description: Counts describe TextUnit and relationship records in the app’s combined graph: a retained first-round 2026 graph plus the October 26 second-round 2026 coded leaf and parent items. Selected supporting-text paraphrases are explicitly identified; the full clarification/task layer and online review Forms/STARS set are not complete. These counts describe graph encoding, not source size, instructional emphasis, or completeness outside the stated scope.

doc:fl-science-2026-draft.coverage: complete first-round leaf benchmark enumeration; historical version retained for comparisons
doc:fl-science-2026-draft.note: This document is the first-round 2026 draft, with 1,512 unique leaf IDs and one aggregate summary row in the historical base graph. Do not read its wording or its reviewed crosswalk edges as October 26 findings. Separate FDOE online review forms/STARS standards are still not represented.

doc:fl-science-2008.note: All 498 unique 2008 benchmark IDs are represented with full text, grade/code, and source locators. The graph also contains one composite legacy crosswalk row assigned to this source by the base graph; use the source-item total (498), not raw TextUnit count (499), as the 2008 benchmark denominator. The 1,494 semantic-neighbor links are machine-ranked leads only.

doc:fl-science-1996.note: The graph contains 170 TextUnits derived from the reviewed 1996 source-first set and crosswalk decompositions. The source-first review enumerates 56 original standards; 170 is not a count of original standards or a 2026 coverage denominator.

doc:fl-science-gle-1999.note: The graph contains 141 TextUnits representing 140 unique GLE codes plus one grade-placement record. This does not represent all historical revision artifacts.

doc:ngss-all-topic-standards.note: All 208 NGSS Performance Expectations are represented with text and PDF/extract locators. DCI descriptions, clarification statements, assessment boundaries, Appendix E progressions, MS-LS evidence statements, and NRC framework materials remain in the corpus but are not all itemized as graph nodes. The 624 semantic-neighbor links are machine-ranked leads only.

doc:external:8f3e333f4967c18a.note: Ten complete grade-level blocks (K–8 and 9–12) are encoded from the 2007 Florida Citizens for Science proposal. The source does not use item codes in this layout; no benchmark-level draft relation is inferred. Its front matter states that FCS claims no copyright interest.

doc:unassigned-source.coverage: 157 derived TextUnits lack a single sourceDocument
doc:unassigned-source.note: These are chiefly composite legacy crosswalk nodes that cite multiple historical source files in their sourceFiles field. They remain visibly unassigned because no single source edition accurately describes the whole composite. This is a data-modeling limitation, not a claim that their source material is unknown.

doc:external:indiana-2000.coverage: complete K–8 item extraction; human comparison incomplete
doc:external:indiana-2000.note: All 412 science statements from the nine ERIC-preserved grade booklets are represented. Three machine-ranked candidate links per item are discovery leads only; human omission review remains incomplete. The 1,236 candidate edges do not establish borrowing or omission.

doc:fl-science-2026-10-26.coverage: complete October 26 leaf and parent-code enumeration; selected supporting-guidance paraphrases
doc:fl-science-2026-10-26.note: The current graph contains 1,573 leaf benchmark IDs and 339 coded parent-standard descriptions. Every leaf is linked to its code parent. Four additional paraphrase nodes highlight Earth age, universe age, common ancestry, and climate change in selected tasks/clarifications; they are not separate standards and do not constitute a complete supporting-text inventory. The current-vs-first-round textual comparison reports 1,463 same-ID identical sentences, 30 same-ID wording changes, and 19 exact-sentence reindexings. Of 61 current IDs new by code, six carry an exact first-round sentence under a different code and 55 have no exact first-round sentence match; this does not mean 61 concepts are new. There are 1,512 shared IDs, zero first-round IDs absent and 61 current IDs new. PDF p.230 SC.8.NT.1.5 was visually confirmed as a code with no separator before “Evaluate”; the October 29 parser was corrected. Exact-string and same-ID links cite the audit crosswalk; they do not establish drafting authorship or source access. The separate FDOE Forms/STARS material is not included.

corpusInventory.note: Counts describe the current private research corpus and its offline LSI index. Copyright-sensitive external source text is retained locally; public graph nodes use citations and short original paraphrases.

graphCounts.note: Effective combined graph after duplicate IDs in the addendum are resolved with primary-graph precedence, matching the app. Structural parent/guidance links, normalized-identifier-only links, and exact-text string matches are counted separately from human-reviewed conceptual comparisons.

portalForms.status: partial capture and source-first reconciliation underway; do not count these in grade-band PDF coverage yet

graphVersionScope: Contains the historical first-round 2026 graph and a separately versioned October 26 second-round node set. Current leaf-to-parent structure is modeled, with four selected supporting-guidance paraphrases. First-round-to-October 26 edges distinguish exact sentence matches, sentence reindexings, and shared-code links with wording changes. New code labels do not imply new concepts. Full clarifications, task/example segmentation, and separate online review Forms/STARS items are not yet a complete graph layer.

currentVersionExtractionReview.correction: Rendered 6–8 PDF p.230 and confirmed SC.8.NT.1.5 is printed without a separator before “Evaluate”; the parser now splits the code and retains the benchmark sentence. The initial word-boundary inventory missed this item. Also recovered SC.912.M.2.1, whose code follows the preceding parent-description sentence on the same extracted line.
